startup.definition: The act of starting a new operation or practice.

founder.definition: To break down, literally or metaphorically.

co-founder.definition: A person who starts an organization, company, or institution together with others. Co-founders share the work of creating it and often retain major ownership or leadership roles.

ceo.definition: The corporate executive responsible for the operations of the firm.

cto.definition: A senior executive sets an organization’s technology direction, system design, and approach to developing new ideas; the title is usually shortened to CTO, meaning chief technology officer.

mvp.definition: The player judged to be the most important to the sport.

pitch-deck.definition: A short presentation that explains a business, product, problem, solution, market, and plan to an audience such as investors or partners.
pitch-deck.exampleUsage: The team revised the pitch deck before the competition.

business-plan.definition: An educational assignment or case study asks students to create a real or imaginary business plan by applying accepted methods and standards.

mission-statement.definition: A concise formal statement explains an organization’s purpose, values, and main goals. It helps members make decisions and shows stakeholders what the organization intends to achieve.

vision.definition: An idea of what an organization hopes to achieve in the future.

seed-round.definition: An early stage of startup financing used to support initial development and growth.
seed-round.exampleUsage: The case study describes a seed round as early startup funding.

series-a.definition: A set of items arranged in a particular order or appearing one after another.

angel-investor.definition: A private person funds a young company in return for a share of its ownership and may provide advice.

venture-capital.definition: Specialized investors finance young, innovative, rapidly growing, or risky firms that cannot yet borrow from banks or sell shares publicly.

crowdfunding.definition: Funding from a large number of small backers.

bootstrap.definition: A strap that is looped and sewn to the top of a boot for pulling it on.

valuation.definition: An appraisal of the value of something.

equity.definition: The difference between the market value of a property and the claims held against it.

dilution.definition: A decrease in an owner's share when a company issues more shares.

term-sheet.definition: A document outlining the main proposed terms of a business investment or financial agreement before final contracts are completed.
term-sheet.exampleUsage: The founders reviewed the term sheet with qualified legal advisers.

traction.definition: (orthopedics) the act of pulling on a bone or limb (as in a fracture) to relieve pressure or align parts in a special way during healing.

user-acquisition.definition: The process of attracting and gaining new users or customers for a product or service.
user-acquisition.exampleUsage: The startup measured the cost of user acquisition.

churn-rate.definition: The percentage of customers or users who stop using a service during a given period.
churn-rate.exampleUsage: The team tracks churn rate each month.

growth-hacking.definition: A business term for rapid, experimental methods aimed at increasing users, engagement, or revenue, often with limited resources.
growth-hacking.exampleUsage: The class discussed growth hacking as a startup marketing concept.

product-market-fit.definition: A situation in which a product strongly meets the needs of a real target market and customers consistently value it.
product-market-fit.exampleUsage: The founders interviewed customers while testing product-market fit.

pivot.definition: The act of turning on (or as if on) a pivot.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

runway.definition: A bar or pair of parallel bars of rolled steel making the railway along which railroad cars or other vehicles can roll.

burn-rate.definition: The rate at which a company spends available cash over a period, especially before it becomes profitable.
burn-rate.exampleUsage: The financial model tracks the startup's monthly burn rate.

disrupt.definition: To change an industry by introducing a new way of doing things.

iterate.definition: To say, state, or perform again.

lean.definition: Using limited resources efficiently while testing ideas quickly.

sprint.definition: A short period of focused work to complete a set of tasks.

standup.definition: A brief meeting or status update in which participants remain standing to keep it focused and short.

retrospective.definition: Concerned with or related to the past.

okr.definition: Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting method that pairs a clear objective with measurable results used to track progress.
okr.exampleUsage: The team set an OKR for improving customer response time.

north-star.definition: A bright star called Polaris lies close to the north celestial pole and has long helped people navigate the Northern Hemisphere.

unicorn.definition: An imaginary creature represented as a white horse with a long horn growing from its forehead.
